message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key rights and protections you have as a tenant in Texas. These rights are derived from state statutes (primarily the Texas Property Code) and some federal laws that apply to residential rentals. | Category | What You’re Entitled To | How It Helps | |----------|------------------------|--------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | Protects your money and ensures you get it back if no damage or unpaid rent exists. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the premises in a safe, livable condition (e.g., plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity).
• Must repair or replace broken fixtures, pipes, or appliances that affect health or safety. | Guarantees a safe living environment. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot interfere with your peaceful use of the property (e.g., excessive noise, unreasonable inspections). | Ensures you can live without constant harassment. | | **Notice Requirements** | • **Rent Increase**: Landlord must give at least **30 days’ written notice** for a rent increase.
• **Termination of Lease**: For month‑to‑month leases, either party must give **30 days’ written notice**. | Gives you time to plan or negotiate changes. | | **Repair and Deduct / Rent Withhold** | • If landlord fails to make necessary repairs, you may:
 1. Pay the repair yourself and deduct the cost from your rent (up to the amount of the repair).
 2. Withhold rent until repairs are made (but only if the issue is serious and you notify the landlord in writing). | Allows you to enforce repairs without breaking the lease. | | **Landlord Entry** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering, except in emergencies. | Protects your privacy. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Under federal Fair Housing Act and Texas law, landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or other protected classes. | Ensures equal treatment. | | **Lease Terms** | • Landlords cannot include clauses that are illegal or that violate your statutory rights (e.g., waiving your right to a habitable dwelling). | Prevents unfair or unlawful contract terms. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow the proper legal process (notice, court filing, judgment).
• You have the right to contest an eviction in court. | Protects you from unlawful eviction. | | **Health & Safety Codes** | • Landlord must comply with local building codes, fire safety regulations, and health codes. | Ensures the property meets minimum safety standards. | | **Tenant’s Right to Repair** | • If the landlord fails to fix a problem that affects health or safety, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from your rent (up to the amount of the repair). | Provides a remedy when landlord neglects duties. | ### Practical Steps If You Need to Exercise Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** – Keep records of all communications, receipts, photos of damages, and copies of the lease. 2. **Written Notice** – Send a written notice to the landlord for any repair requests or disputes. Use certified mail or email with read receipt. 3. **Repair & Deduct** – If the landlord does not respond within a reasonable time, you may repair the issue yourself and deduct the cost from your rent. Keep receipts and document the repair. 4. **Seek Mediation** – Many cities offer free or low‑cost mediation services for landlord‑tenant disputes. 5. **Legal Action** – If the dispute escalates, you can file a claim in small claims court (for amounts up to $20,000) or seek assistance from a local tenant advocacy group. ### Resources - **Texas Property Code** – The primary source of tenant rights. - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** – Offers guidance on security deposits and landlord responsibilities. - **Local Tenant Advocacy Groups** – Provide legal aid, mediation, and education. - **Small Claims Court** – For disputes involving less than $20,000. --- **Note:** This overview is general information and not legal advice. If you face a specific issue, consider consulting a licensed attorney or a local tenant advocacy organization for tailored guidance.
